statements.text: Anvi's frog count can be a population if she counts only frogs in that pond that morning.
Counting frogs and fish together in the same pond still counts as one population.
A count of frogs of the same kind in the pond at one time is a population count.

stem:
Anvi counts the frogs in the school pond one morning. A classmate says this count is a population. A population is a group of the same kind of organisms in the same habitat at a given place and time.

Which statements are correct?

teacher.key_rationale: A population is one kind of organism in one habitat at one time. Frogs alone in the pond that morning qualify; frogs mixed with fish do not make one population.
